verdict.rationale: Knowledge lets agents write and update pages so they can 'learn and self-improve over time.' It also claims to keep itself current from connected sources like Slack and Monday, which suggests some autonomous upkeep. There is no explicit documentation of extracting salient facts from raw conversation, or of a background consolidation or deduplication process run by the memory layer itself. Missing for 10: documented automatic fact extraction from conversation transcripts, background consolidation/merging of memories, details on how salience is decided, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the memory layer decides for itself what is worth remembering — extracting salient facts from raw conversation and consolidating them in the background

citations.quote: With Knowledge, an agent can not only read information but update it too, allowing it to learn and self-improve over time.
You connect the systems where your org already writes, like Slack and Monday, and Knowledge keeps itself current.
For updates, the agent writes the page to the scope that matches the request.
